newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to buy 1.8 mln T Iraq crude under U.N. deal.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to buy 1.8 mln T Iraq crude under U.N. deal.

text.p: Turkish state oil refining company Tupras said on Monday it had signed an agreement with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) to lift a total of 1.8 million tonnes of Iraqi crude under the second term of the U.N.-monitored oil-for-food deal.

"Tupras and SOMO signed an agreement on August 9 for Tupras to buy a total of 1.8 million tonnes of Kirkuk crude oil until December 12, 1997," said the statement. That amounts to about 13.5 million barrels.
"The first delivery will be made on August 20," it said.

Tupras bought 1.9 million tonnes of Iraqi crude under the first term of the oil-for-food deal from December 11, 1996, to June 6 this year and paid $263.5 million to escrow account at the United Nations, it said.
The statement gave no further details.
Tupras used a pipeline from Ceyhan, terminus of the Iraqi oil pipeline from Kirkuk, to its central Turkish Kirikkale refinery for most of its liftings under the first term.
Industry sources said earlier on Monday Tupras would lift 650,000 barrels on August 20 and another 650,000 barrels on August 25 through the Ceyhan-Kirikkale pipeline.
Ceyhan officials earlier said Iraq had about one million tonnes of crude stored at the 12 tanks at the terminal which have a total capacity of about 11.8 barrels.
